messages:
alex: Heads up — the Dedicated capacity dashboard for cust-org 'acme' shows zero nodes/GPU after the cluster resize.
ops: https://console.redwood.ai/dedicated/acme/inventory — looks empty on my side too :grimacing:
maria: timeline? did someone run a manual scale or terraform? any deploys?
alex: autoscaler scaled down 3->1 at 09:12 UTC then terraform apply to move workloads at 09:30 (scale back to 4). Dashboard went blank ~09:35.
jen: can you curl the inventory API?
alex: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://internal-api.redwood.local/v1/dedicated/nodes?org=acme&cluster=eu-west-1"` -> `[]`
sre-bot: alert: inventory_service_shard_mismatch cluster=eu-west-1 severity=warning
liz-oncall: I can take this. Checking inventory-service logs and elastic index health now.
ops: FYI support ticket #INC-2026-148 opened by CSM — customer sees app errors (503) and billing meter shows no GPUs billed after 09:30.
maria: possible causes: index not updated after node metadata change, or a race on node registry write during terraform state change. Also check redis/kafka lag.
liz-oncall: quick findings: inventory-service pod restarted at 09:36 due to OOM, leader-election jittered, and reindex job didn't complete (status: failed). Logs: `ERROR reindex: Shard 3 lost mapping for cluster eu-west-1`
jen: can we force reindex? any safe ad-hoc command?
liz-oncall: running `POST /internal/inventory/reindex?cluster=eu-west-1` now (on staging first). If OK, will run prod reindex with 1% traffic shift.
alex: customer impact: dashboards empty, routing sends to fallback models causing latency spikes. They've escalated to Sales.
ops: pre-checks: disk usage OK, etcd stable, kafka consumer lag=0. The only odd thing is inventory-service had ~200MB RSS spike before OOM.
maria: possible workaround: restart inventory-service deployment gracefully to trigger re-sync with registry. Also add a fallback to query node-registry directly for dashboards if index empty.
liz-oncall: prod reindex started 10:55 UTC. Watchers on metrics: mesh shows node-heartbeats returning data, dashboard still empty until ES index refresh.
jen: nodes reappear on dashboard at 10:58 UTC, but GPU counts are off for node-45 (shows 3 instead of 4).
alex: we confirmed node-45 gpu-plugin crashed during terraform resize. kubelet logs show `nvidia-driver lost` at 09:33.
maria: remediation: scheduled node-45 reboot and redeploy gpu-plugin; also added a post-resize hook to wait for device-plugin readiness before writing node metadata.
ops: mitigation for customers: health-check that returns last-known-good inventory while reindex runs. Filing follow-up ticket to add that.
sre-bot: incident created: INCIDENT-2026-148 severity=sev2 owner=liz-oncall
liz-oncall: will draft postmortem and add automation: 1) scale/resize playbook adjusted, 2) reindex job alerts, 3) OOM thresholds tuned for inventory-service.
alex: thanks all — I notified CSM and customer. Please keep me updated in this thread. :thumbsup:
jen: noted. adding tests to CI to simulate terraform-based node swaps and verify inventory stability.
ops: closing loop: nodes stable and GPU counts reconciled at 11:07 UTC. Will monitor for 24h.
alex: confirmed with customer that dashboards now show correct numbers. Ticket moved to monitoring.
